facts.raw_span: an 18-month history of pain in the plantar aspect of her left foot
the pain was moderate initially, often worse at night, and markedly exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold
three prominent, soft-tissue nodules with swelling and tenderness were palpated in the plantar aspect of the left foot
they were mobile and not adherent to surrounding tissue
numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
toe and foot motor strength were normal
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot demonstrated three nodules arranged in a linear distribution in the mid-plantar region
On T1-weighted images, the lesions were homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle
On T2-weighted fat-suppressed images, they were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration; each was surrounded by a hyperintense rim
a small extension of high signal from the lateral aspect of one lesion resembled a “mouse-tail”
she denied any trauma
no family history of neurofibromatosis
